name: REF6025IDGKR
title: REF60xx precision series voltage reference with built-in ADC reference driver
summary: The REF6025, REF6030, REF6033, REF6041, REF6045 and REF6050 are bandgap series references (2.5 V, 3 V, 3.3 V, 4.096 V, 4.5 V and 5 V) whose output passes through an on-chip wideband buffer with force and sense pins, so a single part can feed the REF input of a precision SAR or delta-sigma converter without a separate driver amplifier. Drift is 5 ppm/°C maximum from -40 °C to 125 °C and initial error ±0.05 %, both for reference and buffer together; output impedance is 50 mΩ typical from DC to 200 kHz with a 47 µF load. The output short-circuit limit is set by a resistor on SS, an enable pin cuts supply current to about 1 µA, and the part comes in an 8-pin VSSOP.

Suffix R is a 2500-piece large reel and T a 250-piece small reel; all are VSSOP-8 (DGK).

circuits.title: 18-bit, 1 MSPS burst-mode data acquisition system
circuits.description: The reference output feeds the REF input of an ADS8881 18-bit SAR converter directly, with no external buffer. OUT_F and OUT_S meet at the top of the output network, a 5 mΩ series resistance in line with a 47 µF capacitor, so the buffer regulates at that point. A 120 kΩ resistor from SS to ground sets the short-circuit limit, a 1 µF capacitor on FILT lowers broadband noise, and EN sits on the supply so the reference is always on. A THS4521 fully differential amplifier with 1 kΩ input and feedback resistors drives AINP and AINN through 5 Ω resistors and a 10 nF differential capacitor, the kickback filter that lets the sampling capacitor settle within the acquisition time.
notes: Design targets: burst-mode support, ENOB above 16 bits, THD below -120 dB, power under 50 mW, 1 MSPS throughput.
Measured: SNR 100.5 dB, ENOB 16.4, THD -125.9 dB, first sample better than 18 bits, 40 mW.

circuits.title: 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz noise measurement setup
circuits.description: The reference runs from a supply decoupled by 0.1 µF with EN tied to VIN, and drives a 22 µF output capacitor. A 40 mF capacitor into a 1 kΩ resistor AC-couples the output into a non-inverting amplifier with a gain set by 10 kΩ and 100 Ω, followed by a band-pass of two high-pass and four low-pass poles spanning 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz, whose output goes to an oscilloscope.
notes: The setup gives no connection for SS or FILT.

operation.text: SAR converters, and some delta-sigma converters, switch binary-weighted capacitors onto their REF pin during each conversion, and the charge taken depends on the input signal. A reference with tens of ohms of output impedance above 100 Hz sags in step with the signal, which shows up as distortion and nonlinearity. The REF60xx puts a low-impedance, wide-bandwidth buffer after its bandgap, so it can drive such a REF pin directly while keeping total noise low.

A bandgap reference, enabled by EN, feeds an internal RFILT resistor whose far end is the FILT pin; the external CFILT forms a low-pass there. That node drives the non-inverting input of the output buffer, which is powered from VIN, drives OUT_F and takes feedback from OUT_S. The bandgap returns to GND_S and the buffer to GND_F. SS sets the buffer's current limit.

Driving the ADS8881 at full rate, the output stays within 1 LSB at 18 bits even on the first conversion after an idle period, so event-triggered, multiplexed, equivalent-time and variable-rate systems get a precise first sample. The buffer restores 70 pC onto a 47 µF capacitor within 1 µs with less than 1 LSB (18-bit) droop. With 1 LSB = 19.07 µV at 1 MSPS, a conventional reference droops by more than 3 LSB within the first 40 µs while the REF60xx stays within one.

Droop is found from ADC codes: a THS4521 drives the ADS8881 with a quiet DC level near positive or negative full scale, the worst case for REF charge. An FPGA captures 1000 bursts of 100 conversions at 1 MSPS, each after a 100 ms idle period, and the 1000 × 100 array is averaged by column, removing the six to seven LSB of converter noise so each column is one microsecond of droop.

Building an equivalent external driver needs four things at once: small offset and drift, broad bandwidth, and a stiff (low-impedance) output. A single OPA350 (38 MHz, 0.5 mV maximum offset, 4 µV/°C) draws 5.2 mA; a composite of an OPA333 for DC precision wrapped around a THS4281 for bandwidth, after a REF5045, takes three devices and many passives and still draws close to 2 mA. The REF60xx is trimmed at several temperatures to reach 5 ppm/°C for reference and buffer together at 820 µA typical.

The REF6025, REF6030, REF6033 and REF6041 are rated for ±4 mA, the REF6045 for ±3.5 mA and the REF6050 for ±3 mA. The output is current limited against shorts; a resistor RSS on SS sets the sourcing and sinking limits (equations 4 and 5) and the recommended load current (equations 6 to 8). SS left open gives 10.5 mA typical; SS tied to VIN gives the highest limit.

The output is stable with 10 µF to 47 µF. At 10 µF the capacitor's ESR must be 20 mΩ to 100 mΩ; at 47 µF, 5 mΩ to 100 mΩ. ESR of 5 mΩ to 20 mΩ can come from PCB trace length alone, without a discrete resistor. Raising ESR above 20 mΩ (below 100 mΩ) widens output bandwidth and improves transient response at the cost of more noise. FILT needs 1 µF for stability and noise.

EN high (1.6 V minimum) selects active mode, needed for normal operation. EN low (0.6 V maximum) selects shutdown: the output goes to high impedance and supply current drops to 1 µA typical. EN draws 100 nA typical at 5 V.

Unequal expansion of the package materials stresses the die when heated and can move the output; reflow soldering is the usual cause. In a test of 128 parts on eight 1.65 mm FR4 boards of 101.6 mm × 127 mm, 16 per board, with lead-free paste and one reflow, every unit shifted by less than 0.03 %. Shift can be higher on boards of other size, thickness or material. Each further reflow adds shift, so where a board sees several reflows the reference goes on in the last one.

Hysteresis is the 25 °C output change after the part is cycled through -40 °C to 125 °C and back. It was measured with parts soldered to a board that had been baked for 30 minutes at 150 °C first; typical values are 33 ppm for the first cycle and 8 ppm for the second.
Noise from 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz grows with output voltage and is 3 µVPP per volt of output for every member of the family.
Dropout voltage is low. At least 0.1 µF goes between VIN and GND_F.

Bypass VIN to ground with a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic. Put CL right next to the ADC, and route OUT_F and OUT_S as two separate traces to CL. Join GND_F and GND_S with a solid plane that also reaches CL; a solid ground plane spreads heat and reduces EMI pickup. Keep external parts close to the device to avoid parasitic errors such as thermocouple (Seebeck) effects. Keep analog traces away from parallel runs with digital ones, crossing them only at right angles when unavoidable. The example layout places CIN, RSS and CFILT around the part with RESR and CL between it and the ADC's REFP and REFM pins, over AGND.
